title: Marked Poisson Minimax Risk for ATE with Validation in the Low-Surrogate Tail
banked_reason: D-0.5 angle 0 ended by explicit --angle-action give-up: revision cap 5 exhausted after reviewer REVISE
gap_reasons: The result is a lone two-point constant lower bound for a newly defined local decision value, without a matching upper bound, a strict published-bound improvement, or evidence that it is the first nontrivial bound for an established estimand.

The claimed first all-rule frontier omits directly relevant MAR functional/minimax work, notably Cheng (1994) on nonparametric mean functionals under MAR and Efromovich (2011) on sharp-minimax nonparametric regression with MAR responses.

The conditional mean is asserted at S(a)=h_n x for every a.e. x>0, including h_nx outside (0,1), without specifying a conditional-law version or the relevant f_a(h_nx)dx-a.e. domain; restrict it to 0<x<1/h_n and state a version/domain convention.
proof_attempt_summary: Five proposal revisions tried to turn a marked-Poisson decision benchmark into an evaluated field-tier frontier. The final proposal gave an optimized two-point minimax lower bound, but the promised finite certificate witness, matching same-class upper bound, and unconditional original-data transfer remained open; the reviewer retained the same frontier objection after the root repair. A future retry needs an audited two-sided infinite-window result or a located strict improvement over an established MAR minimax bound, plus the domain and literature fixes above.
tldr: Under a known exact-power chart-validation design and binary residual marks, the shrinking low-surrogate tail yields a marked-Poisson ATE decision benchmark. The headline theorem restricts the full measurable class to two signed arm-\(1\) profiles, evaluates their equal-prior Bayes risk, retains the zero-count event, and optimizes the support endpoint to prove a positive analytic minimax-MSE frontier with exact scaling \(c_1^{-(\beta+2)/(\alpha+1)}\); at the canonical parameters it is \(e^{-2/3}/16\approx0.03208857\), and the inherited diagonal transfers it to original data. Poissonization, the partition sandwich, tail correction, qualitative diagonal, finite hierarchy, and homogeneity remain inherited conditional infrastructure. A second, explicitly conditional theorem transfers any feasible typed rational certificate through a fourteen-coordinate primitive error ledger to an original-data estimator and an exactly honest randomized interval. The unavailable unit-window rational arrays remain an open finite witness construction, and a second open question asks whether growing annular certificates admit subexponential bit complexity in expected count.
gap: Regular Gaussian efficiency and named-estimator limit laws do not provide an explicit all-rule lower frontier when validation information stays finite in the low-surrogate tail. Generic experiment transfer and convergent finite games also do not join rational feasibility residuals to exact original-data honesty, and the available numerical audit does not serialize a complete rational witness.
fill: The primary theorem derives and optimizes the restriction-to-Bayes-to-zero-count lower chain, including its exact validation-intensity exponent and original-data transfer. The second theorem conditionally specifies finite games, coefficient enclosures, feasibility norms, primitive transfer coordinates, a quantified diagonal, and a reconstructed data rule. The open constructions seek the missing canonical rational witness and scalable annular certification.
